title: Normalized lifting of prescribed vertex equivalences
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. Let $J$ be a small simplicial set, $J_0^{\\mathrm{disc}}=\\coprod_{j\\in J_0}\\Delta^0$, and $D$ a quasicategory. Use equivalence edges and cores as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $r:\\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)^\\simeq\\to\\operatorname{Fun}(J_0^{\\mathrm{disc}},D)^\\simeq$ for restriction. For any core diagram $d\\in\\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)^\\simeq_0$ and any fixed edge $e:\\Delta^1\\to\\operatorname{Fun}(J_0^{\\mathrm{disc}},D)^\\simeq$ with $e(0)=r(d)$, define $\\mathcal L(d,e)_n$ to be the maps $h:\\Delta^n\\times\\Delta^1\\to\\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)^\\simeq$ with $h|_{\\Delta^n\\times\\{0\\}}$ the constant map at $d$ and $rh=e\\,\\operatorname{pr}_2$. Then $\\mathcal L(d,e)$ is a nonempty contractible Kan complex. A vertex supplies a diagram $d'$ with exactly the prescribed terminal vertex values and an equivalence $d\\to d'$ restricting to $e$. Restriction of all simplicial parameters gives the higher comparisons in this same contractible space. The terminal diagram is allowed to vary; only the initial diagram and the entire vertex-equivalence path are fixed.

source.place: Returned Steps 3–4, literal-value normalization and its compatible choices; HTT Sections 2.1.2 and 2.4.6 (exponentiation and equivalence lifting) Argument extracted from the returned proof; HTT supplies the background constructions, not a verbatim assertion of this formulated lemma. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison.

proof.text: Put $A=J_0^{\mathrm{disc}}$. Its canonical map $i:A\to J$ is degreewise injective: an $m$-simplex of $A$ is the constant simplex at a vertex $j$, and restricting its image along any vertex of $\Delta^m$ recovers $j$. Apply the restriction clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] with $A\hookrightarrow J$ and the given quasicategory $D$. Thus $R:\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,D)$ is an isofibration between quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration] to $R$. Its induced core map is exactly the stated restriction $r:E\to B$, where $E=\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)^\simeq$ and $B=\operatorname{Fun}(A,D)^\simeq$, so $r$ lifts every horn, including the outer horns.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3, followed by Proposition 4.4.3.7 (01EZ; also read in Subsection 4.4.3, 01CZ).

proof.text: Write $I=\Delta^1$. The defining equations for $\mathcal L=\mathcal L(d,e)$ are preserved under precomposition by $\Delta^m\times I\to\Delta^n\times I$ induced by every simplex operator. They therefore define a simplicial set. More generally, a simplicial map $T\to\mathcal L$ is precisely a map $H:T\times I\to E$ such that the restriction of $H$ to $T\times\{0\}$ is constant at $d$ and $rH=e\operatorname{pr}_I$: in degree $m$, evaluation sends a pair consisting of an $m$-simplex $t$ of $T$ and an $m$-simplex $s$ of $I$ to $H_t(\operatorname{id}_{[m]},s)$. Conversely, restriction to each simplex $t:\Delta^m\to T$ recovers $H_t$. These operations are inverse and commute with operators, by the definition of the internal functor simplicial set in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Paragraph 2, normalized coherent diagrams in the inverse-limit mapping-space calculation; explicit agent expansion of simplicial parameters.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and a boundary $u:\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal L$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Step 2 gives its family $H_\partial:\partial\Delta^n\times I\to E$. On $\Delta^n\times\{0\}$ prescribe the constant map at $d$. These maps agree on $\partial\Delta^n\times\{0\}$, hence glue degreewise to a map from $K_n=(\partial\Delta^n\times I)\cup(\Delta^n\times\{0\})$ to $E$. Its image under $r$ equals $e\operatorname{pr}_I$, since this holds on the first piece by the defining equation and on the second by $e(0)=r(d)$. The inclusion $\{0\}\hookrightarrow I$ is the horn inclusion $\Lambda_0^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, so it has the left lifting property against all Kan fibrations. The inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] to these two maps: the resulting map $K_n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times I$ is anodyne. As $r$ is a Kan fibration by Step 1, it supplies a filler $H:\Delta^n\times I\to E$ with $rH=e\operatorname{pr}_I$, extending both prescribed pieces exactly. Step 2 identifies $H$ with a simplex of $\mathcal L$ filling $u$. For $n=0$ this is a lift of $e$ with initial vertex $d$, so in particular $\mathcal L$ has a vertex.

source.place: SSet.anodyneExtensions_pushoutObjObjι, lines 95-103; explicit boundary lifting square, including dimension zero.

proof.text: Step 3 proves that $\mathcal L\to\Delta^0$ has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion, including $\partial\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. The boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] makes this map a trivial fibration in the Kan--Quillen model structure. In particular it is a Kan fibration and a weak homotopy equivalence for the geometric-realization meaning fixed there. A Kan fibration to $\Delta^0$ is exactly a Kan complex, and the weak equivalence to $\Delta^0$ is exactly contractibility in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Together with the dimension-zero filler this gives all three assertions: nonempty, Kan, and contractible.

source.place: Definition Tag 08NL (label definition-trivial-kan, lines 5533-5545) for the boundary convention; the existing Kan--Quillen-model node supplies the weak-equivalence characterization.

proof.text: Let $h$ be a vertex of $\mathcal L$. It is an edge $d\to d^{\prime}=h(1)$ in the core $E$, hence an equivalence of coherent diagrams by the core definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The exact equation $rh=e$ gives both its prescribed vertex-equivalence path and $r(d^{\prime})=e(1)$ as equalities of simplicial maps; no replacement of terminal vertex values by merely equivalent values has occurred. For any simplex operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the family associated to the restricted simplex is $h\circ(\Delta(\alpha)\times\operatorname{id}_I)$. It still has initial value $d$ and projects to the entire fixed path $e$. Thus all parameter restrictions and all higher comparisons are those of the same Kan complex $\mathcal L$, whose contractibility was just proved. The equation at $t=1$ constrains only the vertex restriction of the terminal diagram; the terminal diagram itself has never been fixed.

source.place: Paragraph 2, literal vertex normalization and compatibility of choices; explicit extraction from the defining equations.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2; explicit normalized lift-space argument using existing isofibration/core, pushout-product and Kan--Quillen-model nodes. Online Kerodon 01F3 and 01CZ checked; archival copies WANTED.
